dedupe_keys.name: usgs global rare earth element occurrence database

description: This U.S. Geological Survey geodatabase documents rare earth element deposits and occurrences worldwide, with mineralogy, deposit type, host and associated rocks and ages, alteration, and resource and production sizes and grades where public. The ScienceBase page says the Global_REE feature class holds about 3,100 located deposits and occurrences, a non-spatial table holds 820 without a known location, and more than 1,590 references are stored in a references table; rare earths here include the lanthanides and yttrium. It was published on 22 March 2018 by Greta Orris, Yuna Seo, Deborah Briggs, Pamela Dunlap and Mark Cocker, and is downloadable as a file geodatabase of about 95 MB, a shapefile, Excel workbooks, an introduction document and metadata, free under CC0 1.0 according to the DataCite record, with global coverage. Caveats: records are compiled from literature of very different ages and quality, and many lack size or grade, so they describe occurrences, not producing mines. For simulation it maps where rare earth supply could come from, for magnet and electronics supply chain concentration and disruption scenarios and for hazard exposure of REE regions. Related catalogue records include the EURARE rare earth occurrences in Europe, the USGS global critical minerals distribution and the USGS Critical mineral deposits of the United States.
